content:
Over the past year, everyone has been eagerly awaiting the arrival of the next-generation iPad mini, and reports suggest it is just around the corner. New information leaked by Aaron Perris last week shows that the new device will feature an A20 Pro chip and slimmer bezels; in addition, we already know it will sport an OLED display and a waterproof design.

While these upgrades are certainly appealing, my main expectation for the next iPad mini actually has to do with software.

After seeing iPhone Duo, I was amazed at how well Apple managed multitasking. To me, multitasking on the iPad has always felt messy, but iPhone Duo handles it with elegance and smoothness.

On a screen this small, the iPad mini has never really been ideal for true windowed mode. Users rarely stack multiple windows on the iPad mini. So I hope Apple can take a cue from iPhone Duo and add a practical feature: split-screen combined with picture-in-picture.

Highest-rated comment posted by Mathew Ledbetter

You make a great point, and it echoes my biggest frustration; the software on the iPad mini is just a shrunken-down version of the larger iPad. Apple doesn't seem to have put much thought into tailoring the experience for this screen size. The home screen widgets are so small you can barely see them, and the number of icon rows you can place is very limited, wasting a huge amount of empty space. The whole experience is really poor.

Honestly, this experience could be done so much better. Currently on the iPad mini, the picture-in-picture window cannot span the full width of the screen in portrait mode; even if it could, you'd still have to cover part of the app or manually resize the window yourself.

To me, bringing split-screen video and app viewing to the iPad mini's display is almost a given, especially since the aspect ratios of the iPhone Duo and iPad mini are so similar. With this feature, I would at least be far more willing to use the iPad mini in portrait mode.
